title: 2019 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 Coupe 3ZR ZTK

scenes.headline: 755 Horsepower
scenes.narration: 755 horsepower and 715 pound-feet of torque—that’s the Corvette ZR1's heart-pounding reality. Beneath its aggressive hood vent, the ZR1 churns out incredible power from a supercharged 6.2-liter LT5 V8.

scenes.headline: Race Legend
scenes.narration: The 2019 Corvette ZR1 marks the pinnacle of seventh-generation Corvettes, reclaiming the Nürburgring record with a blistering 7:04 lap time, underscoring its prowess on the track and street alike.

scenes.headline: Downforce Heavyweight
scenes.narration: With a huge rear wing and front splitter, the ZTK package produces over 900 pounds of downforce at top speed, helping it stick to the tarmac like glue.

scenes.headline: Carbon Fiber Focus
scenes.narration: The eye-catching carbon fiber supercharger cover isn't just for aesthetics; it supports the Corvette ZR1's focus on weight reduction and performance.

scenes.headline: $120K -> $150K
scenes.narration: Starting at $120,000 new, the 2019 ZR1 now trades around $150,000 today, showcasing a rare 4% annual appreciation for such high-performance beauties.

scenes.headline: Quarter Mile King
scenes.narration: In a head-to-head showdown, the ZR1's 10.8-second quarter-mile eclipses the Porsche 911 GT3's 11.0 seconds, revealing its agile dominance.

scenes.headline: Viewer Choice
scenes.narration: So, would you take the beastly 755-horsepower ZR1 for a spin, or does its raw power seem like overkill?

script: 755 horsepower and 715 pound-feet of torque—that’s the Corvette ZR1's heart-pounding reality. Beneath its aggressive hood vent, the ZR1 churns out incredible power from a supercharged 6.2-liter LT5 V8. The 2019 Corvette ZR1 marks the pinnacle of seventh-generation Corvettes, reclaiming the Nürburgring record with a blistering 7:04 lap time, underscoring its prowess on the track and street alike. With a huge rear wing and front splitter, the ZTK package produces over 900 pounds of downforce at top speed, helping it stick to the tarmac like glue. The eye-catching carbon fiber supercharger cover isn't just for aesthetics; it supports the Corvette ZR1's focus on weight reduction and performance. Starting at $120,000 new, the 2019 ZR1 now trades around $150,000 today, showcasing a rare 4% annual appreciation for such high-performance beauties. In a head-to-head showdown, the ZR1's 10.8-second quarter-mile eclipses the Porsche 911 GT3's 11.0 seconds, revealing its agile dominance. So, would you take the beastly 755-horsepower ZR1 for a spin, or does its raw power seem like overkill?
